newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGOSLAV TEAMS IN CROATIAN CHESS TOURNEY.
newsitem.headline: YUGOSLAV TEAMS IN CROATIAN CHESS TOURNEY.

text.p: Two Yugoslav woman's chess clubs plan to take part in a tournament in Croatia this week, the first teams from what remains of Yugoslavia to compete there in any sport since the former federation broke up, state news agency Tanjug reported on Sunday.
Partizan and Gosa women's chess clubs, last year's Yugoslav champions and vice-champions, will take part in the European chess champions cup in Rijeka, on the Croatian coast, on June 20-22.
"Preparations are underway for the departure of our two teams to participate in the championship in Rijeka," Belgrade's Partizan chess club director Bozidar Rajacic told Reuters.

"The Yugoslav Chess Federation left it up to the individual clubs to decide if they will participate. We have decided to go," Rajacic said but added they would know definitely in a day or two when all formalities are completed.
"We will probably be the first sports team from Yugoslavia to play in Croatia," he said.
The tournament is organised by Kastav chess club from Rijeka which addressed official invitations to the Yugoslavs.

Besides Partizan, Gosa and Kastav, the tournament will group representatives of Ukraine from the Grandmaster chess school of Kiev, Romanian champion Venus, British champion Slug and two German teams Elberfelder and Universitaetssportsverein from Halle.
The Yugoslav Chess Federation decided not to participate in a European chess tournament in Croatia last May.
Due to political tensions following the break-up of the former Yugoslavia in 1991, most sports contacts between newly formed states of the former Yugoslavia have had to take place in third countries.
